clue.text: Pretty maids bleeding in the garden

definitions.meaning: attractive young women, beauties, are lovely ones
...-bleeding is a garden plant, so these letters come before 'bleeding' in a flower bed's name

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is not a true synonym: it points at the plant love-lies-bleeding, whose name begins with the answer and continues with 'bleeding'.
explanation.definitionFit: Beauties are called lovelies, and the amaranth love-lies-bleeding grows in gardens.

clue.text: Bird, gets incentive from flower

parts.note: the lark is a songbird
a spur is an incentive or goad

explanation.surface: A songbird is encouraged by a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Delphinium is a tall garden plant with spurred blue blooms.

clue.text: Triumphant Scot of an earlier age

parts.note: a victor is the triumphant one in a contest
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A Scotsman who won his battles long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian is the Scottish form of John, so crosswords use it for a Scot.
explanation.definitionFit: Belonging to the 19th-century era of Queen Victoria, hence old-fashioned.

clue.text: Drink, pal

parts.note: the word for friend, written upwards in this down light, would read as lap going up

explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer read as an instruction, LAP written going UP, produces PAL in a down light.
explanation.definitionFit: To swallow eagerly, as a cat drinks milk with its tongue.

clue.text: She is preceded by him initially

definitions.text: She is preceded by him initially

parts.words: She is preceded by him initially
parts.note: HIM, the initials of Her Imperial Majesty, come before this woman's title

explanation.walkthrough: Her Imperial Majesty is abbreviated H.I.M., so this ruler is styled 'HIM' before her title.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman ruling an empire, or an emperor's wife, styled Her Imperial Majesty.

clue.text: Betting experts step on board at intervals

definitions.note: the squares a counter steps along on a board game, laid out at intervals

parts.note: SP, starting price, is the betting odds on a horse at the start of a race
aces are experts at something

explanation.surface: Gambling pros climb aboard a ship or train now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Betting' reads as gambling; here it is SP, the starting price in British horse-racing betting.
explanation.definitionFit: The marked squares on a game board are its places, each a move along.

clue.text: Town official makes harbour on Ladybird

indicators.note: in a down light the first piece is placed on top of the second

parts.note: a port is a harbour
a reeve is the female of the ruff, a wading bird, so a lady bird

explanation.surface: A council officer builds a dock beside an insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ladybird' is not the beetle: a reeve is a female ruff.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval borough's chief magistrate or bailiff.

clue.text: Stop inside man

definitions.meaning: a punctuation mark, a kind of pause in writing
the large intestine, inside a person's body

explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation mark of two dots, and the main part of the large intestine.

clue.text: He aims to find a fortune at the ball

definitions.text: He aims to find a fortune at the ball

parts.words: He aims to find a fortune at the ball
parts.note: suggests a gold-digger at a dance, but describes a crystal-gazer telling fortunes

explanation.walkthrough: The ball is a crystal ball, not a dance, and the fortune is foretold, not married.
explanation.definitionFit: A seer foretells the future by gazing into a crystal.

clue.text: It's time to pay the balance

definitions.meaning: deferred payment, buying now and paying later
the sum in hand in an account

explanation.definitionFit: Buying on tick gives deferred payment, and an account's positive sum is in the black.

clue.text: Flimsy material Eric revised essay

indicators.note: something revised has been reworked, so the name's letters are rearranged

parts.note: an essay set at school or college is a paper

explanation.surface: Eric has rewritten his essay, but it is still thin stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' turns ERIC into RICE; a school essay is a paper.
explanation.definitionFit: This edible thin sheet is a delicate, see-through stuff used in cooking and art.

clue.text: Sovereign principle it's right to follow

indicators.note: the letter for right is told to come after the word for principle

parts.note: a rule is a principle or guideline

explanation.surface: A moral maxim says it is proper to obey.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch, king or queen, governs a realm.

clue.text: Lower oneself to hawkish conduct

definitions.meaning: to condescend, bend down to something beneath you
a hawk's dive on its prey from a height

explanation.definitionFit: To condescend is to bend down morally, and a falconer's bird dives steeply on quarry.

clue.text: Lasting quality in Provence river, say locals

parts.note: EN is French for in, as people in Provence say
the Durance is a river flowing through Provence in southern France

explanation.surface: Something durable found along a river in southern France, as the residents tell it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say locals' tells you to use the French word: EN is what people in Provence say for 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is the capacity to hold out or keep going over time.

clue.text: These ones may be dramatic

parts.note: ones as single wholes; the classical theatre rules of time, place and action are three of them

explanation.walkthrough: A unity is a oneness, and Aristotle's dramatic unities are the rules of a single time, place and action in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: The three classical stage rules are time, place and action, each a oneness.

clue.text: To perform off the cuff is better all round

indicators.note: the word for better goes all the way around the little word

parts.note: to better something is to improve it

explanation.surface: Playing without a script is better in every way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' looks like an adjective praising the performance, but it is a verb here, and 'all round' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To extemporise, making something up on the spot.

clue.text: The mail ship has gas-heating units

parts.note: RMS stands for Royal Mail Ship

explanation.surface: A postal liner carries the means of measuring gas.
explanation.walkthrough: A therm is a unit of heat once used for billing gas in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: British gas was charged by heat delivered, measured in units of 100,000 BTU.

clue.text: Impart motion with this expedient

definitions.meaning: to make something move, cause a shift

explanation.walkthrough: Split in two, the answer reads 'make shift', to cause movement.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopgap is a temporary substitute, and causing a shift sets something moving.

clue.text: Action without purpose caused loss of dignity

indicators.note: the old sense of without is outside, so the word for action goes around

parts.note: a deed is an action
a mean, as in means to an end, is a purpose

explanation.surface: Doing things aimlessly made someone look foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowered someone's standing, humiliated them.

clue.text: Fowler as a marksman?

parts.note: a fowler hunts birds; one who hunts the snipe would be named after it, and the word also means a sharpshooter

explanation.walkthrough: A fowler who shoots snipe (a wading bird) can be called by this word, which also means a hidden marksman.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharpshooter fires from cover, and the word also suggests a hunter of the snipe bird.

clue.text: Having underground radical connexions

parts.note: sounds like links to a secret revolutionary group, but describes a plant fixed by roots

explanation.walkthrough: Radical comes from Latin radix, root; the underground connections are a plant's roots, not a resistance cell.
explanation.definitionFit: Fixed firmly in soil by a plant's roots.

clue.text: A spot of colour

parts.note: a small dot or fleck marking a surface

explanation.definitionFit: A fleck or small mark of a different hue on a surface.

clue.text: Relationship of Milton's Voice and Verse

definitions.text: Relationship of Milton's Voice and Verse

parts.words: Relationship of Milton's Voice and Verse
parts.note: in Milton's poem At a Solemn Music, Voice and Verse are called the 'sphere-born harmonious' pair of female siblings

explanation.walkthrough: Milton's 'At a Solemn Music' opens 'Blest pair of Sirens ... Sphere-born harmonious sisters, Voice and Verse'.
explanation.definitionFit: Female siblings, as Milton names the pair Voice and Verse.

clue.text: Transposing halves by proxy is correct

indicators.note: the two halves of the phrase swap places, back half to the front

parts.note: per pro, Latin, means acting on behalf of another, as in signing letters

explanation.surface: Signing for someone else is legitimate if the halves are swapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transposing halves' turns PER PRO into PRO PER.
explanation.definitionFit: Right, fitting or according to the rules.

clue.text: Ruins our corn, as spiteful as can be

indicators.note: ruining the words wrecks their order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A vandal spoils a farmer's crop out of sheer malice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruins' rearranges OUR CORN AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Full of bitter ill-will and resentment, as malicious as possible.

clue.text: London was Spenser's most kindly

parts.note: Spenser's Prothalamion calls the city 'my most kindly' one who brought him up

explanation.walkthrough: A completion of Spenser's Prothalamion: 'To mery London, my most kyndly Nurse'.
explanation.definitionFit: Spenser names London as the carer who raised him.

clue.text: As pedantic as teaching class in this

indicators.note: the answer sits within this run of clue words, across the joins

explanation.surface: Lessons given in a fussily academic way suit this social group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in this' points into the clue itself: pedantiC AS TEaching.
explanation.definitionFit: A hereditary social rank, as in the Hindu system.

clue.text: The case for the ton-up boys ?

definitions.text: The case for the ton-up boys ?

parts.words: The case for the ton-up boys ?
parts.note: a case is a box, and slang for an old motorbike or car is the same word

explanation.walkthrough: Ton-up boys were British 1960s motorcyclists who rode at 100 mph; an old banger of a machine is slang 'crate', also a packing case.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden packing box, and slang for an old vehicle.

clue.text: Left in France for the match

definitions.meaning: a person seen as a good marriage prospect

explanation.definitionFit: In French it means gone away; in English it is an eligible suitor.

clue.text: The height of joy about victory-day revolution

indicators.note: the word for joy is placed around the other piece

parts.note: elation is great joy

indicators.note: a revolution turns the abbreviation round, so it is written backwards

parts.note: VE Day was Victory in Europe Day, 8 May 1945

explanation.surface: Peak happiness at the turn of a wartime victory celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' turns the victory-day abbreviation backwards; VE Day was the British name for the 1945 Allied victory in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Altitude, height above sea level or ground.

clue.text: Smoker's jacket?

parts.note: the phrase suggests a smoking jacket, but the word means a cannabis cigarette and also a short double-breasted coat

explanation.walkthrough: One word covers both: a marijuana cigarette that a smoker smokes, and a heavy double-breasted jacket worn by sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a cannabis cigarette, and the name of a naval coat.

clue.text: Gave agreement as transmitted to editor

parts.note: something transmitted has been sent

explanation.surface: Someone agreed to the piece as it was submitted to the editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Consented, said yes.
